answer_text:
We evaluate the limit by factoring out the dominant power of \(n\) from each term.

Since \(n\to\infty\), we may assume \(n>0\).

\[
L=\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\sqrt{n+2}-\sqrt{n^2+2}}
{\sqrt[4]{4n^4+1}-\sqrt[3]{n^4-1}}
\]

Divide both numerator and denominator by \(n\):

\[
L=
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\dfrac{\sqrt{n+2}}{n}-\dfrac{\sqrt{n^2+2}}{n}}
{\dfrac{\sqrt[4]{4n^4+1}}{n}-\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{n^4-1}}{n}}
\]

Now simplify each term.

### Numerator

\[
\frac{\sqrt{n+2}}{n}
=
\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sqrt{1+\frac{2}{n}}
\to 0
\]

and

\[
\frac{\sqrt{n^2+2}}{n}
=
\sqrt{1+\frac{2}{n^2}}
\to 1
\]

So the numerator tends to

\[
0-1=-1.
\]

### Denominator

\[
\frac{\sqrt[4]{4n^4+1}}{n}
=
\sqrt[4]{4+\frac{1}{n^4}}
\to \sqrt[4]{4}=\sqrt2
\]

and

\[
\frac{\sqrt[3]{n^4-1}}{n}
=
n^{-1/3}\sqrt[3]{1-\frac{1}{n^4}}
\to 0.
\]

So the denominator tends to

\[
\sqrt2-0=\sqrt2.
\]

Therefore,

\[
L=\frac{-1}{\sqrt2}=-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}.
\]

\[
\boxed{-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}}
\]
